title: Clarinetists and Raymond Burke at the Club Plantation
summary: Hug recalls clarinetists and Raymond Burke's band at the Club Plantation.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Who were some of the clarinet players you remember as outstanding? We've already mentioned Aaron and now. Harry Shields.

Harry Shields. Bill Bourgeois. Of course, Raymond. Raymond Burke. And then, of course, to get back to piano players, another fine piano player just entered my mind. A little fella that used to play with Raymond at the Club Plantation. Oh, Julia Chavez. Mm-hmm. Julia Chavez was a good, very good, very good jazz piano player. Played very nice style. He played with Raymond quite a while at the, when it was Pete Hoyman's Club Plantation. Henry with Henry Walde. That was a real good little swinging little band. They used to go in and listen to them? Yeah. Oh, they used to come on the air every night in those days. That was back about 30 or 31. Raymond used to play his harmonica. I think they used to use a theme song. Raymond came on with his harmonica solo. Some kind of a real weird, wild solo. But it was a real good little band. Really swung in those days.
Raymond was real outstanding then. Boy, he played some wonderful clarinet with him. With his band.
It's funny how he never got recognition until-
Until later years. Until later years. That's right. Well, of course, that's the same old story as the jazz story. So many men that were lost until later years. Bill Bourgeois.
Bill Bourgeois, that's right. He told me how he always missed getting recorded. He would always come last time. That's right.
